content.text: **Finding: compliant (at fallback).** Section 14.3 selects California law with domestic AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco — an accepted jurisdiction and a domestic forum, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 14.3 Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California.
input.rationale: Section 14.3 is the sole governing law, venue and dispute clause (Section 12 escrow disputes are referred back to it). It selects the laws of the State of California, which is an expressly accepted law under the fallback position, and the dispute forum is domestic: single-arbitrator AAA commercial arbitration seated in San Francisco County, California, with judgment enforceable in the San Francisco courts. This is neither the vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue nor mandatory arbitration seated abroad, so it is well clear of walk-away territory. The clause therefore sits at the fallback (California law and a California forum) rather than the preferred New York law / New York County courts position. The only sub-preferred sub-element is that the forum is domestic arbitration rather than courts; because the seat is domestic and the law is accepted, we note this in the rationale rather than flagging it as a deviation, and we do not redline. Neutral, non-directional clause binding both parties equally.
